title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 26 (Matters to be stated in prospectus)

content.overview: Section 26 governs the content and formal requirements of a prospectus issued by or on behalf of a public company (or by or on behalf of any person engaged or interested in the formation of a public company). Every such prospectus shall be dated and signed and shall state such information and set out such reports on financial information as may be specified by the Securities and Exchange Board in consultation with the Central Government. Until SEBI so specifies, SEBI regulations under the SEBI Act in respect of such financial information or reports apply. The prospectus must also contain a declaration about compliance with the Act and a statement that nothing in it is contrary to the Companies Act, the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956 and the SEBI Act and the rules and regulations thereunder. A signed copy must be delivered to the Registrar for registration before the prospectus is issued. A prospectus is not valid if issued more than ninety days after the date on which a copy was delivered to the Registrar.
content.glance: Dated and signed; SEBI-specified information and financial reports (or SEBI regulations until specified); compliance declaration; ROC filing before issue; not valid if issued more than 90 days after delivery to Registrar.
content.study:
Section 26 is the principal content and formality provision for prospectuses.

Statutory test
1. Scope: every prospectus issued by or on behalf of a public company (formation or subsequently), or by or on behalf of any person engaged or interested in the formation of a public company.
2. Dating and signing: the prospectus shall be dated and signed.
3. Content: state such information and set out such reports on financial information as may be specified by SEBI in consultation with the Central Government; until so specified, SEBI regulations under the SEBI Act apply.
4. Compliance declaration: declaration about compliance with the Act and a statement that nothing in the prospectus is contrary to the Companies Act, SCRA 1956 and SEBI Act and rules/regulations.
5. Filing: signed copy delivered to the Registrar for registration before the prospectus is issued.
6. Validity period: prospectus is not valid if issued more than ninety days after the date on which a copy was delivered to the Registrar.
7. Expert statements and consent: additional rules apply where the prospectus includes a statement purporting to be made by an expert.
8. Application: subject to sub-section (2), the provisions of sub-section (1) apply to a prospectus or a form of application whether issued on or with reference to formation or subsequently. The date indicated in the prospectus is deemed to be the date of its publication.

Boundary
Section 26 is about what must be stated and the formalities of dating, signing and filing. Section 25 is about when an offer-for-sale document is deemed a prospectus. Listed or intending-to-list issues also attract SEBI ICDR and related regulations as the practical source of required disclosures under the SEBI-specification mechanism.

sections.heading: Dating, signing and SEBI-specified content
sections.body: Every prospectus within section 26(1) shall be dated and signed and shall state such information and set out such reports on financial information as may be specified by SEBI in consultation with the Central Government. Until SEBI so specifies, SEBI regulations under the SEBI Act apply.

sections.heading: Compliance declaration
sections.body: The prospectus shall make a declaration about compliance with the provisions of the Act and a statement that nothing in the prospectus is contrary to the Companies Act, the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956 and the SEBI Act and the rules and regulations made thereunder.

sections.heading: Filing with Registrar and validity
sections.body: A signed copy must be delivered to the Registrar for registration before the prospectus is issued. A prospectus is not valid if issued more than ninety days after the date on which a copy was delivered to the Registrar.

sections.heading: Expert statements
sections.body: Where the prospectus includes a statement purporting to be made by an expert, the expert’s written consent and other statutory conditions apply.

provisions.title: Matters to be stated in prospectus

examples.title: Compliant prospectus
examples.body: A public company dates and signs its prospectus, includes SEBI-specified information and financial reports, makes the compliance declaration, and delivers a signed copy to the ROC before issue, within the ninety-day validity window.

examples.title: Stale prospectus
examples.body: A prospectus is issued 100 days after a signed copy was delivered to the Registrar. Under section 26 it is not valid.

hypotheticals.question: Is dating alone enough for a valid prospectus?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 26 also requires prescribed content (SEBI-specified information and reports), signing, compliance declaration, and delivery of a signed copy to the Registrar before issue, within the ninety-day validity period.

distinctions.title: Content of prospectus (s. 26) vs deemed prospectus (s. 25)
distinctions.left: What must be stated and formalities
distinctions.right: When an offer-for-sale document is treated as a prospectus

misconceptions.trap: A short advertisement is always enough without a full prospectus.
misconceptions.correction: Public offers require a prospectus meeting section 26 requirements (and applicable SEBI regulations).

misconceptions.trap: The long original statutory list of prospectus contents still applies unchanged.
misconceptions.correction: Section 26(1) as amended requires such information and reports as SEBI may specify in consultation with the Central Government; until specified, SEBI regulations under the SEBI Act apply.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 26 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify the prospectus and whether it falls within section 26(1). II. Check dating, signing, SEBI-specified content, compliance declaration and ROC filing. III. Check the ninety-day validity rule. IV. Apply expert-consent rules if relevant. V. Conclude.

bareActPointers: SEBI ICDR and related regulations where applicable
examTips: Separate formality (date, sign, file) from content (SEBI-specified information and reports).
Always mention ROC filing before issue and the ninety-day validity rule.
